scope: Actual operational page lifetime, configured clock skew, stopped Control policy/TTL change, current dataset grants and account-triggered session revocation. Bounded evidence, not complete discovery, management editors, capacity, M1 or release.

environment.postgres: PostgreSQL 16.15 (Debian 16.15-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit fsync=on full_page_writes=on

artifacts.input_equivalence: All non-documentation/experiment build inputs equal except 12 enumerated unused frontend inputs. Reused f677 Rust pair and original 4e signed seed retain their identities. No fresh Rust compilation or frontend execution.

workload: Fresh signed archive seed, successful empty export, actual upgrade through 0816 and five signed-event HTTP acceptances under deliberate 256 MiB deferral. Six jobs, one in-memory login across two Controls. Accepted policy3 explicitly uses 12-second cursor TTL and two-second skew; policy4 uses five seconds and zero skew. Default production settings are unchanged.

executed.local: Syntax, artifact, complete diff and actual caller INCOMPLETE/FAIL/PASS propagation checks PASS. No product code change or unrelated suite rerun.

invariants.lifetime: Actual server-issued first cursor and both ordinary/grace continuations retain the original issue and expiry. Reading within the configured two-second grace returns the expected page; first and continued cursors return410 after that same absolute deadline. Full retention row/xmin stays unchanged during this sequence. A fresh listing gets a new 12-second deadline and changes only retention deadline/xmin.
invariants.skew: The independent documented 103-byte payload and libsodium1.0.18 encryption create two authenticated future-issue fixtures from the actual original token. Within-skew succeeds before its issue instant; outside-skew returns400 while independently observed SQL time remains more than two seconds before issuance. Their other decoded fields match the actual token. This tests envelope clock checks without changing a host clock; it is not clock-jump recovery evidence.
invariants.policy: Actual Control stops with release, then a privileged isolated SQL fixture appends policy4 and restarts the same installed binary. The old still-unexpired policy3 cursor returns409. Fresh policy4 issuance has five-second TTL and zero-skew expiry returns410 within the old two-second grace interval. The longer prior key retention row and xmin stay identical; a shorter new obligation neither reduces nor unnecessarily rewrites it. This does not qualify a production policy editor or live rollout.
invariants.grants: Privileged dataset/account-locked fixture changes remove data.read while retaining status.read, remove status.read, then restore it. Exact grant-row deltas and one account grant revision per change are independently checked. Old bindings return409; fresh status-only pages succeed; revoked access returns403 for both an otherwise live token and malformed bytes. Restoring access permits a new list while old bindings remain incompatible. The fixture does not implement or qualify a dataset-grant editor.
invariants.session: Account deactivation advances authentication revision once and revokes exactly three previously live Alice sessions in the same xmin, with revocation times bounded by independent SQL clocks. Other account/session rows and all idle/last_seen values remain unchanged. Requests with a still-live cursor and malformed bytes then return401 and preserve the new session state. Ordinary read/restart/grant boundaries preserve full projected session timestamps/xmin.
invariants.durable: Ten complete job/admission/input/export/unit/artifact/file/lease/pin/claim projections including xmin agree at seven saved boundaries and final. Each of nine successful pages matches independently reconstructed full SQL-derived item fields and every decoded binding. Auth/policy/session changes are attributed separately. Both Controls stop with release, parent absent/destination flock available; final actual Control/catalog backend counts are zero.

review.root: Read actual domain codec, page adapter, request/error and dispatch boundaries plus affected fixtures/guards. Confirmed pinned official libsodium encryption ABI. Preserved preparation logs using distinct lifetime prefixes; checked403literal and grant effects. Independently rechecked captured page sets, clock windows, policy/retention and session transitions, all safe payload hashes, exact Git input and reused ELF identities, and live resources.
review.ai: Read-only pre-run fixture review found three setup/oracle gaps: hard-coded ready3 after policy change, unchanged-session claim after the actual revocation trigger, and missing complete retention comparison after TTL reduction. All corrected and reread; no further concrete blocker in that scope. No AI tests/SSH or post-run evidence review.

not_qualified: No raw host-clock jumps, expiry/revocation during socket delivery, dropped policy notice/live restrictive rollout, standalone logout boundary or arbitrary grant races qualified by this profile.
Backdated/tied real pages, delivery/resource exhaustion and mixed/aged workloads remain open, as do complete CLI/browser/accessibility, M1, native arm64 and release journeys.

PostgreSQL wrapper137 without OOM is owned deadline cleanup, not graceful PostgreSQL restart evidence. Native runner0. All original databases, logs and artifacts retained; secret configuration, key material and token bytes excluded from safe capture.
